caveats: Basis differs by source: Ember (all countries + US regions) = lifecycle gCO2/kWh of generation; MEE China factors and OpenElectricity SWIS = direct combustion CO2 only. Lifecycle values typically run ~5-15% above direct for fossil-heavy grids.

Ember US state dataset gives a lower US total (345.8 g/kWh in 2024) than the Ember global dataset for the USA (383.8 g/kWh; the global file applies generic lifecycle factors per fuel). US regional values are internally consistent but ~10% below the methodology used for other countries.
US ISO/regional values are aggregates of state in-state generation, not true balancing-authority footprints, and ignore imports/exports (notably California imports, Arizona nuclear exports).
China values are MEE consumption-based regional/provincial averages for 2023 (latest published); China dec uses the Ember national trend as a proxy.
Australia (au) is the WA SWIS grid, not national Australia.
All CI values are annual averages of generation; the hourly or marginal intensity faced by a new data-centre load can differ substantially.

dec is a backward-looking 2015->2024 CAGR (2015->2023 for SWIS), not a forecast. Hydro-dependent grids (Pacific NW, Brazil) are volatile year to year; Brazil CI rose in 2024 vs 2023 but fell over the decade.
The task mentions 28 regions but lists 25 ids; this file covers those 25 (75 values).
